VERIFIED real facts (handle with NUANCE/RESPECT, never mockery): In 1974 (West Germany) Zaire - today's DR Congo - became the FIRST Black African / sub-Saharan / Central African nation ever to reach a World Cup finals, as reigning African champions, the Leopards (AFCON winners 1968 as Congo-Kinshasa and 1974 as Zaire - two titles). The tournament turned cruel (a 9-0 loss to Yugoslavia). The infamous Mwepu Ilunga moment v Brazil (~78', score 2-0): he burst out of the wall and booted the free kick away before it was taken, earning a yellow; for decades commentators mocked the clip as 'African ignorance'. The truth told later: dictator Mobutu had the squad threatened over how heavily they were losing, their bonuses withheld; Ilunga has said he acted in protest / to be sent off - a frightened man, not a clown. PORTUGAL: Euro 2016 champions, still chasing a first World Cup; Cristiano Ronaldo is 41, this his sixth and final World Cup, the one trophy he has never lifted. lines.text: In nineteen seventy-four, a defender ran out of the wall and booted a free kick away — and the whole world laughed at him.
They called it ignorance. They were wrong. And tonight, his shirt walks out again — with someone in the stands who knows the real story.
Last time, we predicted Austria would edge Jordan two-one. Tonight, a forty-one-year-old legend collides with the ghosts of the Leopards.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-four. Portugal versus DR Congo. The chase for a first crown… against the men who opened a continent's door.
And stay with me — because at the death, the oldest man on the pitch settles it.
First, the history. And this one is true. West Germany, nineteen seventy-four. A nation then called Zaire.
They were the first Black African team ever to reach a World Cup. African champions — the Leopards, kings of their continent.
But the tournament turned cruel. Nine-nil to Yugoslavia. And back home, a dictator was watching, and seething.
Mobutu had the squad threatened over how badly they lost. Their bonuses, taken. These men were playing in fear.
So against Brazil, Mwepu Ilunga charged from the wall and hammered the ball away — a yellow card, on purpose. A protest no one understood. It was never ignorance. It was courage.
That is the shirt DR Congo wear tonight. Not a punchline — a door, kicked open for a whole continent.
Across from them: Portugal. European champions in twenty-sixteen — but a World Cup has always slipped through their fingers.
Bruno Fernandes unlocks any door. Bernardo Silva, all silk and cunning. Rafael Leão flies down the left, and Rúben Dias is a wall in dark red.
And leading them, one last time — Cristiano Ronaldo. Forty-one. Sixth World Cup. The one trophy he has never lifted.
But the Leopards did not come to make up the numbers.
Yoane Wissa, sharp and fearless. Cédric Bakambu, who has scored on almost every continent he has played.
Chancel Mbemba marshals the back — a captain who has tamed strikers across Europe.
Silas Katompa carries it forward, Arthur Masuaku gives them steel. A young, hungry team with an old, proud soul.
So here is the duel. Portugal's golden chase… against the spirit of the Leopards.
Our prediction — built on Portuguese class, on Congolese pride, and on one old king who is not finished yet. Watch.
Portugal press first. Bruno threads it, Leão burns the line — the cross is cut back, and the Seleção strike. One-nil.
But you cannot tell the Leopards it's over. Bakambu spins, Wissa is away — and the door swings open. One-all. Listen to them sing.
Then Portugal find another gear. Bernardo's pass splits them apart.
And Leão is there to finish — two-one, Portugal.
And at the death — of course — it is him. Ronaldo rises, one last time. Three-one, in our story.
Portugal three, DR Congo one — our prediction. The chase goes on, and the Leopards walk off with their heads held high.
Do you agree? Comment SELEÇÃO if Ronaldo finally lifts it. Comment LEOPARDS if the door swings open again.
And the man in the stands? Legend number twenty-four: the Leopard. He stood in that wall in seventy-four.
He carries the yellow card that was never shame — only courage. Tonight his Leopards run again. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings you to WorldCup twenty-six dot world. Pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score… scores for you.
Free to play. Live prize pool. Underdogs like the Leopards pay triple. Hit like, send this to a friend — and subscribe. The legends are only beginning.
